title: Hydrolytic Synthesis and Structural Characterization of Lanthanide Hydroxide Clusters Supported by Nicotinic Acid

synthesis.procedure: One-pot ligand-controlled hydrolysis: a mixture of 10 mL of Eu(ClO4)3 (1.0 M) and nicotinic acid (0.62 g, 4 mmol) in 15 mL of deionized water was stirred at 90 °C while aqueous NaOH (1.0 M) was added dropwise to the point of incipient but permanent precipitation. The mixture was refluxed for 1 h, filtered hot, and the filtrate cooled to room temperature. Block-shaped colorless crystals formed after 1 week.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the same one-pot procedure as 1, replacing Eu(ClO4)3 with Gd(ClO4)3. Aqueous mixture of Gd(ClO4)3 and nicotinic acid was pH-adjusted with 1.0 M NaOH at 90 °C to incipient permanent precipitation, refluxed 1 h, filtered hot, and crystallized at room temperature as block-shaped colorless crystals.

synthesis.procedure: Two-step synthesis: with stirring, 1.0 M NaOH was added dropwise to 10 mL of Eu(ClO4)3 (1.0 M) at 90 °C to incipient permanent precipitation. Separately, 1.0 M NaOH was added to nicotinic acid (0.62 g, 4 mmol) in 5 mL of deionized water to pH 8. The nicotinate solution was added dropwise to the pH-adjusted lanthanide solution. The mixture was stirred at 90 °C for 1 h, filtered hot, and the filtrate stood at room temperature for 2 days to give block-shaped colorless crystals.
